name: Druids of the Fang
summary: In the Wailing Caverns, the Druids of the Fang pursue their design. These rogue night elves severed ties with the Cenarion Circle and took serpent forms under Lord Serpentis. Their true origin remains a mystery to outsiders. They seek to seize the underground waters and remake the Barrens as their own paradise.

sections.title: A Noble Vision Turned Poisonous
sections.body: Naralex led young druids into the Wailing Caverns to restore the Barrens. The land had once been a lush sanctuary, and he hoped to bring it back. Beneath the caverns, they reached natural fissures and springs. Naralex entered an induced slumber to channel the living energies of the Emerald Dream into those waters. He hoped to revive the scorched savannah above.

sections.title: Descent into Nightmare
sections.body: Within Naralex's trance, a malevolent nightmare took hold where the Emerald Dream's serenity should have been. Its darkness spread through the caverns, warping the wildlife and poisoning the underground springs. Naralex's acolytes did not flee to seek help from the Cenarion Circle. The nightmare overwhelmed them, changing their minds and spirits along with the life beneath the earth.

sections.title: The Fang Ascendant
sections.body:
Naralex's prize pupil had once been a devoted student. He cast aside his master's teachings and embraced the corruption as Lord Serpentis. He gathered the fallen acolytes into the Druids of the Fang and took the venomous forms of vipers and serpents, rather than the bear and cat forms Cenarius sanctioned.

The Fang hold their sleeping master captive and seek to feed on his nightmare. They would remake the Barrens as a paradise ruled by serpents.

faq.q: Who are the Druids of the Fang?
faq.answer: The Druids of the Fang are night elf druids who entered the Wailing Caverns under Naralex. The nightmare in his trance drove the acolytes mad and transformed them into fanatical snake-worshiping renegades.

faq.q: Why did they enter the Wailing Caverns originally?
aliases: why are they in wailing caverns
faq.answer: Naralex and his acolytes entered the Wailing Caverns to reach its underground springs. They hoped to channel the Emerald Dream's vitality through the waters and turn the arid Barrens back into a thriving green forest.

faq.q: Who leads the Druids of the Fang?
faq.answer: Lord Serpentis leads the Druids of the Fang. Once the foremost and brightest of Naralex's students, he fell into madness when the nightmare struck and declared himself leader of the new order.

faq.q: What animal forms do they take?
faq.answer: The Druids of the Fang take the forms of venomous serpents and vipers. They embrace serpentine magic and vicious snake forms instead of the bears, cats, or stormcrows of traditional Cenarion Circle druids.

faq.q: How does the Cenarion Circle view them?
aliases: are they part of the cenarion circle
faq.answer: The Cenarion Circle sees the Druids of the Fang as a dangerous aberration and cult. Elders such as Nara Wildmane of Thunder Bluff and Naralex's loyalists work urgently to eliminate the Fang's leaders and cleanse the corruption before it destroys the land.
Naralex lies trapped in a deep, agonizing slumber in the heart of the Wailing Caverns. His disciples keep him confined and use his ongoing nightmare to warp the caverns and their own magic.

angles.text: As a druid, the Druids of the Fang show the peril of corruption in the Emerald Dream. They show what follows when a druid abandons Cenarion harmony for twisted, unorthodox animal forms.
As a tauren, you share Nara Wildmane and Thunder Bluff's concern with ending the Fang's threat. Their defilement of the Barrens' water affronts the Earth Mother.
As a night elf, seeing kaldorei kin become a feral, nightmare-ridden snake cult in the heart of Kalimdor brings sorrow and shame to your traditions.
